newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa sees 1996/97 budget on course.
newsitem.headline: South Africa sees 1996/97 budget on course.

text.p: The South African department of finance said on Friday in a half-year report on the course of the 1996/97 budget that most targets appeared likely to be met, including the deficit of 5.1 percent of GDP.

"Figures for the six months April to September 1996 show that the 1996/97 budget remains on track and that the budget targets including the deficit of 5.1 percent, before borrowing, of estimated GDP should be achieved unless major unforeseen developments occur," a statement said.
It said exchequer requisitions for the period amounted to 85.5 billion rand, 12.8 percent higher than the previous year.
The figure represented 49.2 percent of the full year's budget estimate, against a ratio of 48.1 percent at the same stage last year.
Exchequer receipts during the first six months were 69.2 billion rand, 16 percent higher than the previous year.
This represented 47.8 percent of estimated revenue for the full financial year, compared with 46.8 percent half-way through the previous year.
"During the first six months of the financial year, loans of 22 billion rand were entered into," the statement said, adding that this did not include a recent mark loan of 1.49 billion rand.
"The 22 billion rand is some 49.0 percent of the total expected borrowing required for the year," the statement said.
